newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Liberia's postwar election fixed for July 19.
newsitem.headline: Liberia's postwar election fixed for July 19.

text.p: West African heads of state have postponed Liberia's post-war general elections to July 19 instead of May 30.

An official communique at the end of their talks in the Nigerian capital Abuja on Wednesday said the delay was requested by Liberian leaders who said the the original date, May 30, was no longer feasible because of logistic and security problems.

"They approved that the election day will be Saturday 19th of July 1997 with the inauguration of the new government on 2nd of August, 1997," said the communique after the one-day summit of the committee of nine, an Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS) group overseeing Liberia's peace agreement.
If a run-off were needed, it would be on August 2 and the new government inaugurated on August 16th.

The 16-nation ECOWAS brokered the end of Liberia's seven-year civil war last year and the presidential and legislative vote will consolidate the peace enforced by a Nigerian-led West African peace-keeping force called ECOMOG.
Liberian leaders, including former warlords now presidential candidates, have called for a postponement of the vote until August or September.
"We hope that this meeting will be the last to be held for the resolution of the Liberian crisis," Nigerian military ruler General Sani Abacha told the closing session of the Abuja summit.
"This election will lead to the restoration of full democracy in Liberia," Abacha, the chairman of ECOWAS, added.
Among those present were the presidents of Ghana, Burkina Faso, Mali, Niger and Benin. Others sent representatives.
Abacha said the costs of the polls had been cut by half to $4.1 million. Taiwan had donated $1 million "without strings attached" while Ghana gave ballot boxes.
West African leaders had argued against delaying the polls for too long, saying that could disrupt the peace process in Liberia.
"It is important that we do not do anything to dislocate the progress made so far," Ghana's President Jerry Rawlings told the Abuja summit.
Freed American slaves founded Liberia in 1847. The war has killed more than 150,000 people and displaced half the pre-war population of 2.5 million.
Hundreds of thousands of Liberians are refugees in neighbouring Ivory Coast, Guinea and Sierra Leone. Others are in Ghana and Nigeria.
